Research maps below are structurally capped; every cap stamps a `_trimmed` note naming what it dropped. Full archive: full_context_path.

_pack_budget.note: Measured line budget for this pack. Your Read tool returns ~2000 lines by default; anything starting past that is NOT read unless you page to it with Read(offset=N). Every input that can BLOCK a proposal is above that line by construction, so a default Read is sufficient to answer every gate. The entries below are what you did NOT get — page to them when a name matters.

run_depth_note: Light check: holdings + watchlist prices and news; exits allowed; no full scan; new BUYs discarded.

hard_limits.note: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every threshold the validator enforces, read live from autonomy_config.json this run. Any number quoted in CLAUDE.md prose is DESCRIPTIVE — when the two disagree, these values win, because these are the ones the code actually checks. (CLAUDE.md stated RR >= 1.0 for two days after the floor was raised to 2.0 on 2026-07-16, so every proposal built against the prose was rejected on arrival.)

position_sizing._notional_cap_note: Notional ceilings only. Risk-based sizing below is the binding constraint: a tight-stop setup may size up to these ceilings for the same 1% risk; a wide-stop setup sizes well under them. Raised from 10%/$1000 when risk-based sizing landed (2026-07-16). Rebased 10x DOWN on 2026-07-21 when the book was restated from a $10,000 start to a $1,000 start: every percentage stays identical, only the notional ceilings moved ($2000 -> $200, conviction $3000 -> $300, min clamp $200 -> $20). See _fractional_stop_note below — the smaller book changes what the broker can protect.

risk_based_sizing._note: Van Tharp / Elder / Turtle framework (research 2026-07-16, user-approved). Every BUY risks at most risk_per_trade_pct of equity measured entry-to-stop; the validator CLAMPS oversized proposals down to the risk budget rather than rejecting. Portfolio heat = sum over open positions of entry-basis committed risk max(0,(avg_cost-stop)*qty)/equity; new BUYs are rejected past portfolio_heat_cap_pct (user chose 8%; literature 6-10%). Theme cap: committed initial risk sharing one demand_driver <= theme_initial_risk_cap_pct. Entry-basis heat means trailed stops above cost free the budget (pyramiding into winners stays possible). momentum_unwind_risk_scale halves the risk budget when momentum_health flags an unwind.

scale_in._note: Adds allowed only into winners (price above blended cost, never averaging down), max 2 adds, combined exposure stays inside the per-name cap. Partial exits via sell_fraction in (0,1].

conviction_tier._note: When earned, conviction raises the RISK budget to 1.5% (and the notional ceilings accordingly); base tier stays 1%.

position_sizing._fractional_stop_note: CONSEQUENCE OF THE $1,000 BOOK, measured 2026-07-21 against the live 187-name universe. Alpaca carries fractional quantities only with time_in_force=day, so a GTC stop needs a whole-share leg (execution/alpaca_broker.py, MIN_WHOLE_SHARES_FOR_LIMIT=4 and _resting stop arming). At a $1,429 position (the $10,000 book) 69.5% of the universe got a full exchange-held GTC stop attached at entry and only 2.1% fell under one share. At a $143 position (this book) those become 3.2% and 72.2%: most entries are now sub-one-share, so their protective stop is a DAY order that expires at the close and is re-armed by scripts/stop_watch.py on the Actions cron. Intraday protection is a real resting broker order and is essentially unchanged; what is lost is the overnight/weekend leg, where the exit now depends on the poller's next tick rather than the opening print. Accepted deliberately: the gap risk is real but denominated in single-digit dollars at this size. Do NOT read a low whole-share count as a reason to skip a setup.

quality._variant_perception_note: Every BUY must state the market's misunderstanding explicitly: what consensus believes, what the agent believes differently, the specific mispriced mechanism, and the event/date when the market finds out. Enforced as a required BUY field; format documented in CLAUDE.md.
quality._risk_map_scenarios_note: risk_map and scenarios were always in the CLAUDE.md schema but not validator-enforced, so proposals omitted scenarios and the published scenario_ev stayed empty. Now required on every BUY.
quality._thesis_invalidators_note: Binding falsifiers (not vibes): object with invalidating_print, invalidating_structure, time_box — each a non-empty string. Enforced on every BUY so re-underwrites have kill criteria.
quality._demand_driver_note: Primary demand-driver theme for theme concentration (e.g. hyperscaler_server_capex, ai_compute_gpu). Distinct from GICS sector. See tools/demand_drivers.py and context bundle demand_driver_map.
quality._required_sell_fields_note: SELL_TO_CLOSE needs only these; the BUY-oriented required_proposal_fields list used to reject legitimate discretionary exits for missing stop_loss/target_price. Prefer also exit_reason when available (process, not hard-required).
quality._claim_grounding_note: Added 2026-07-25, DEFAULT OFF pending evidence, same staged rollout as _tradeability_note below. WHAT IT DOES: validator._check_claim_grounding greps every entity a BUY's variant_perception/catalysts name against the FULL context bundle and rejects the ones that appear nowhere in it. Built from four real incidents the LLM risk desk caught by hand: DDOG 07-22 ('JMP Securities raised its target to $311' - the string 'JMP' appears ZERO times in that day's bundle), MELI 07-24 ('Loggi acquisition', a Citi fair-value cut, '14 new Brazil fulfillment centers'), IBKR 07-22 (an invented 'fourth consecutive beat' with an EMPTY guidance_ledger), UNP 07-24 (a 'binding MOU signed one day earlier' that inverts the actual sequence). WHY IT IS NOT ON YET: CLAUDE.md step 5 makes WebSearch MANDATORY before any BUY, so the brain is REQUIRED to bring in facts that legitimately are not in the bundle - blocking on 'absent from bundle' would reject true WebSearch findings alongside fabricated ones, and a false rejection costs a real trade on a book that has already gone days without one. Until proposals carry per-claim sources, the SAME computation is fed to the risk desk every run (validator.unsourced_claims -> runlib.brain_io), which can weigh the WebSearch context a regex cannot. TO ENABLE: watch the risk-desk prompt's UNSOURCED CLAIMS block for a week; if the entities it lists are consistently real fabrications rather than WebSearch-sourced truth, flip this to true. Precision was tuned against the 7 real BUY proposals in journal/proposals + journal/rejected: multi-word candidates are only taken from an explicit attribution pattern ('<Firm> raised/said/cut'), because the bare proper-noun pass produced prose fragments like 'MINIMUM CONTRACTED' and 'Case After Strong' that no bundle would ever contain verbatim.
quality._min_rr_note: Raised 1.0 -> 2.0 (2026-07-16, user-approved after expectancy research): breakeven win rate at 2:1 is 33%, keeping the book profitable across the realistic 40-55% band; a 1:1 floor loses money below ~52% wins after costs (Minervini/O'Neil both demand ~2:1 at entry).
quality._volatility_stop_note: A stop tighter than the name's noise is not protection - it exits on ordinary volatility, not on a broken thesis. The stop must sit at least max(min_stop_atr_multiple x 14d-ATR%, min_stop_expected_move_fraction x options expected_move%) below entry. Enforced only when volatility data is present (fail-open). If that floor exceeds max_stop_loss_distance_pct, the name is too volatile for a valid swing stop and is rejected.
quality._trailing_stop_note: Chandelier exit (LeBeau/Elder; user-approved 2026-07-16): once a position's high-water mark puts (high_water - 3xATR) ABOVE the plan stop, the effective stop ratchets up with it - never down, never widened, and deliberately NO breakeven jump at +1R (research shows early breakeven moves gut trend expectancy). Forced exits fire on the effective stop; reason trailing_stop_breached when the trail was binding.
quality._falsifiability_note: ADDED 2026-07-19 (audit). variant_perception, scenarios and thesis_invalidators were PRESENCE-checked only, while CLAUDE.md twice called variant_perception 'validator-enforced' - a single non-space character satisfied it. min_invalidator_chars was 12, so 'drops below 50dma' (17) passed as a binding falsifier. scenarios' probabilities need not have summed to 1, and tools/scenario_ev.py computed honest EV whose only callers were two RENDERING paths. Now: invalidating_print needs a numeric threshold, time_box needs a date or day-count, variant_perception needs a figure and a dated resolution, and scenario probabilities must sum to ~1 with a non-negative probability-weighted return. These check SHAPE, not argument quality - no regex grades a thesis, and the risk desk and the reader remain the judges of that.

theme_risk._note: Market value of positions sharing the same demand_driver plus proposed size must stay under this fraction of equity. Catches DELL+HPE style single-factor books that sector caps miss when names sit in different GICS sleeves. Fail-open if demand_driver missing (field check already rejects). The notional cap here complements the RISK-based theme cap in position_sizing.risk_based_sizing.theme_initial_risk_cap_pct.

regime_gate._note: Coded regime filter (Faber 2007/2013: ~halved max drawdown over a century; user-approved 2026-07-16). When the benchmark trend is hostile (SPY below its 200DMA), new BUYs are REJECTED (regime_gate_spy_below_200dma) - exits and holds are never blocked, and existing stops keep working, consistent with the evidence that the filter's value is blocking NEW risk, not forced liquidation. Momentum-unwind detection (tools/momentum_health.py) separately halves the risk budget via position_sizing.risk_based_sizing.momentum_unwind_risk_scale rather than hard-blocking. Fail-open when regime data is absent from market_context.

book_risk._tradeability_note: Added 2026-07-19, both DEFAULT OFF pending evidence. Both floors currently fail OPEN on missing data: a proposal on a ticker absent from market_context skips the stop noise-band check entirely (a 1% stop on an 8%-ATR name passes), and a name with no market-cap figure clears the $1B floor by default. The enforcement is built and tested; enabling is a one-line flip once the evidence is in. require_volatility_data: a live gather covers 182/187 tickers with ZERO universe names absent, so the coverage case is already strong - held off only because 26 existing tests pass market_context={} and rewriting that many safety fixtures hours before going live is how a real assertion gets weakened by accident. Enable after a week of runs, then fix the fixtures deliberately. require_market_cap_data: weaker case and it stays off longer. market_cap_usd is NOT a bundle field (0% coverage there); orchestrator.py resolves it PER PROPOSAL from deep_fundamentals, then scan rows, then a LIVE lookup - so a yfinance hiccup would block every BUY in the run. Blocking the whole book on a network blip is a worse failure than the fail-open it replaces, and the weekly universe review already bars sub-$1B names from entering. Enable only once per-proposal resolution is observed at ~100%.
book_risk._note: Book-level risk (added 2026-07-19 after an audit found every binding constraint was arithmetic on ONE proposal while portfolio_beta / shared_left_tail / corr_to_book were computed by tools/correlation.py and consumed only as prose). Four controls, all in tools/book_risk.py, all pure. (1) max_factor_stack_pct: aggregate notional across factor_map.AI_STACK_DRIVERS. The 2% per-driver risk cap permits ~2 positions per driver, so 8 positions across 4 AI-stack drivers was 100% AI exposure passing every existing limit - a per-driver cap is not a factor cap. (2) gap_adjusted_heat: the 8% heat cap sums (cost-stop)*qty, which assumes stops FILL AT THE STOP - contradicted by execution_costs.stop_gap_atr_fraction (0.5) in this same file, and by the only closed stop in the ledger (DELL plan stop 408.00, fill 389.75, 4.5% through, realized -13.5% on a position sized for 1%). Heat now adds the modelled gap-through, using correlation only to decide how much of the book gaps on the same morning - NEVER to hand budget back, since the plain sum is already the fully-correlated case. Unknown correlation assumes the worst. (3) max_portfolio_beta: MV-weighted against EQUITY not invested capital, so a half-cash book reads as half-exposed. (4) stress_scenarios: named shocks priced against the book the proposal WOULD create; losses deliberately NOT floored at stops, because a shock worth naming is one where stops gap. driver_shocks key __ai_stack__ shocks the whole factor group. All four fail CLOSED on unverifiable inputs, matching the portfolio_heat_unverifiable precedent.

learning_controls._note: Code-enforced Learning Protocol. Under min_trades_for_binding: no hard rejections from calibration_gate. At/above: high-conf inflation caps confidence; losing sector/theme buckets require calibration_exception text. Shadow book binds caution at 8 closed shadows (separate).
learning_controls._target_calibration_note: Added 2026-07-19. min_risk_reward_ratio (2.0) is the system's most rigorously justified rule - the config carries the expectancy math - and it is computed from the LLM's own target_price, which appears ZERO times in execution/exit_guard.py. Exits are stop, trail or horizon only; CLAUDE.md calls the target 'a milestone, not a tripwire'. So the gate filtered on a number nothing enforced or graded, and the model could always clear it by writing a bigger one. Targets stay NON-BINDING for exits (letting winners run is correct and literature-supported) - instead every close is graded on claimed RR vs REALIZED RR and target attainment. Binds only at min_trades_for_binding closed trades; at n=2 it reports phase 'anecdote' and withholds the binding-grade number entirely.

process_checklist.note: Required reasoning order every run. Work top-down; do not propose a BUY before completing the steps above it. Cite the relevant context-bundle blocks in commentary when a step changes your aggression.

steps.title: Macro regime check
steps.must: Read macro_regime (+ market_events / market_news tape). State whether the regime supports adding long swing exposure. Hostile or rolling leadership -> raise the bar, prefer cash / exits.

steps.title: Portfolio / book review
steps.must: Re-underwrite every open position with fresh research: HOLD or SELL_TO_CLOSE. Thesis broken = exit. Cash test: if remaining expected return no longer clearly beats cash yield, rotate. Honor stops, stall flags, and forced-exit aftermath.

steps.title: Idea selection
steps.must: From universe_scan / watchlist / tape promotions, pick at most a handful of candidates. Prefer fat pitches over marginal RR. Empty proposals with a clear no_trade_reason is a valid outcome.

steps.title: Entry geometry & underwrite
steps.must: For each candidate: charts, volume, stop/target geometry, fundamentals freshness, filings, catalysts. WebSearch mandatory before proposing a BUY. Variant perception required. Size and RR must clear validator floors as a MINIMUM, not a target.

steps.title: Kill conditions
steps.must: State what kills the trade and how you would know early (risk_map). Pre-plan stop, horizon, and invalidation before size. If kill conditions are fuzzy, do not buy — watchlist it.

lessons.text: ** Two process gaps cost research time today. First, candlestick charts did not render this run — `data/charts/` was empty even though the gather log said "rendering candlestick charts..."; the chart step appears to depend on the same blocked live yfinance feed rather than falling back to the relay bundle the way the rest of the pipeline does, so I judged entry geometry on numeric indicators alone with no visual confirmation of the actual price bars. Second, the watchlist-trigger-alert logic flagged AMD as "price trigger reached" when the price was actually 3.9% away from my stated $555 level

recent.topic: Reading the consolidation base to define a precise, auditable pivot trigger — and why the throwback to the level, not the breakout through it, is the higher-expectancy swing entry
recent.summary: The base-and-pivot framework (O'Neil's cup-with-handle, Minervini's VCP) exists to convert a fuzzy 'wait for confirmation' into ONE auditable price level: the pivot — the base's prior peak / handle high, the last ceiling of overhead supply. A valid VCP base shows 2-3 successive contractions where BOTH price range AND volume tighten, each smaller than the last, signaling sellers drying up; the classic entry then buys as price clears the pivot on volume ~40-50% above average. But the empirical record undercuts the 'chase the volume breakout' half. Bulkowski's pattern database (reported ~40,000+ trades on thepatternsite.com; I could not fetch the primary page directly and cite these figures as reported by secondary summaries) finds throwbacks occur ~50-60% of the time overall and ~74% when the breakout comes on ABOVE-average volume, and that ~97% of upward-breakout pattern TYPES perform BETTER when no throwback occurs — the strongest breakouts run away and never offer a second chance, while high-volume 'confirmed' breakouts are precisely the ones that throw back most. My own 12-year ablation says the same from the entry side: confirmed_breakout (new 20d high on >=1.5x volume) scored -0.32pp ATR-matched at 21d and ADX>25 breakouts were negative in 10 of 12 years, while the low-volume no_supply_pullback was the ONE positive read (+0.22/+0.25pp). Practitioner consensus reconciles this: buying the throwback/retest to the pivot (now acting as support) on drying volume gives a better
recent.how_to_apply: For every watchlist name, read its base and write the PIVOT — the prior peak / handle high, cross-checked against anchored_vwap — as the would_buy_at level, plus an explicit event-date gate when a catalyst window applies, which fixes the AMD compound-trigger-fired-5-days-early defect (LP-0693555695). Prefer the entry my own data rewards: the throwback to that pivot on drying, no_supply_pullback volume (KB-6241168493), with the stop just below the base low so it sits beyond the sqrt(t) noise band (KB-2388376284) and the 2:1 RR floor clears honestly because I am buying AT the level, not extended above it. Do not make the volume breakout my primary entry and do not reject a setup because its breakout was unconfirmed — confirmed_breakout scored -0.32pp and breakout volume is descriptive-only. When a genuine fat pitch is running away in a supportive tape with a catalyst forcing urgency, take a 50-70% starter on the breakout and add on the retest rather than chasing full size or missing it. recent.topic: Kelly-fraction intuition for the 1% risk budget: why deep-fractional Kelly is correct under parameter uncertainty, and how it explains the 2:1 RR floor and the conviction tier
recent.summary: The Kelly criterion f* = W - (1-W)/R maximizes long-run geometric growth (E[log wealth]) and outputs the fraction of capital to RISK - which maps exactly onto this system's 1%-of-equity, entry-to-stop budget. Running it on my own realistic parameters (2:1 RR floor so R is about 2, swing win rates 40-55% per CLAUDE.md) gives full-Kelly risk fractions of 10% (at 40% wins), 17.5% (45%), 25% (50%), and 32.5% (55%). So the 1% budget is roughly 1/10 to 1/30 of full Kelly - deeper than even quarter-Kelly - and that is correct, not timid, for three compounding reasons the literature is unanimous on. First, parameter uncertainty: MacLean-Thorp-Ziemba showed a 10% overestimate of edge causes about 50% overbetting at full Kelly, the penalty for overbetting FAR exceeds the cost of underbetting, and Thorp always ran fractional Kelly in practice; with only 2 closed trades my true edge is essentially unknown, and Kelly with unknown edge says bet near zero. Second, the growth-rate curve is a downward parabola g(c*f*) approximately (2c - c^2)*g_max: half-Kelly captures about 75% of maximum growth at half the position size, quarter-Kelly about 44%, growth hits ZERO at 2x Kelly, and beyond 2x it goes negative into near-certain ruin - so the over side has a cliff the under side does not, making underbetting strictly the safer error. Third, Kelly assumes independent bets; correlated simultaneous positions share ONE Kelly budget (the multivariate form is f* = inverse-covariance times excess return
recent.how_to_apply: Keep sizing every BUY at the 1% risk budget and read it as intentional deep-fractional Kelly, not caution to apologize for: with 2 closed trades my edge is unmeasured, so betting small IS the mathematically correct response to unknown edge, and I should stop treating the 1% floor as a bar that makes setups feel too small to bother taking. When tempted to argue for the conviction tier (1.5%), require what Kelly requires: a genuinely higher, PROVEN edge (the validator's 15 trades + 55% win rate in the 0.70+ bucket, confidence >=0.75, zero risk-desk haircut, corroborating evidence) - never step up the fraction on a narrative, because the overbetting penalty is asymmetric and a wrong edge estimate over-allocates hard. Treat the 2:1 RR floor as non-negotiable expectancy geometry, not paperwork: below it there is no positive Kelly fraction to size, so never widen a stop or inflate a target to scrape past it. On correlated adds, remember co-moving names share one Kelly budget - the 8% heat and 2% theme-risk caps are that constraint, so size the pair as one bet (KB-1223831607) rather than two independent 1% risks. recent.topic: The options-implied expected move and earnings IV crush: reading options_signals to time swing entries around binary prints, and why the implied move is a market-priced noise band
recent.summary: Options price a stock's expected move as Price × IV × √(DTE/365) ≈ one standard deviation; a fast earnings shortcut is ~0.85 × the ATM front-month straddle (tastytrade uses a weighted straddle+strangle version). Empirically the stock stays inside that ±1σ band ~68-70% of the time, so the implied move is a genuine, horizon-scaled noise band — not a forecast of direction. Crucially it is priced too WIDE on average: implied vol exceeds realized vol by roughly 3-5 percentage points annualized (the volatility risk premium), and a CBOE study of ~10 years of S&P 500 earnings found the actual post-print move was SMALLER than the straddle-implied move in ~72% of cases. But the distribution has fat tails — the ~30% of moves that break the band include the outliers that gap through any stop (the SMCI ~20% preliminary-print pop is exactly this tail). Before a known binary event, front-month IV inflates and the term structure goes into BACKWARDATION (near-term IV > far-term); the moment the event resolves, IV crushes 30-50% (40-55% on high-IV names like NVDA/TSLA) within hours and the term structure normalizes. For a directional trader, holding a swing stop THROUGH a print means betting on a coin-flip gap you are not paid to take: the pre-print premium is a cost to option holders, but to an equity holder the print is just an un-stoppable jump on top of the normal diffusion. The cleaner trade is around it — enter 1-2 days after the print once the gap settles, IV has crushed, and the direct
recent.how_to_apply: Before any BUY, read options_signals.expected_move_pct and term_structure together with days_to_earnings: if a print (or a backwardation + high-iv_rank event premium) falls inside holding_horizon_days, default to trading AROUND it — either enter after the print once IV crushes and the gap settles, or shorten the horizon so the stop never has to survive the binary, because the earnings expected move is a discrete jump no ATR-floored stop inside the 15% cap can cover (this refines KB-2388376284: the implied move is a market-priced noise band, superior to ATR×√N, and stop_engineering already floors the stop at ½ the expected move — treat that as a one-day floor, not horizon-adequate through an event). Only hold through a print when the binary itself is the thesis (a stated drift/gap_held_revisions_up setup per KB-2596574918), and then size on gap-adjusted risk. Use term-structure backwardation and iv_rank as the detector that fired wrong on AMD — an elevated front-month event premium 5 days out means the setup is NOT live yet, so suppress the trigger until the event passes. recent.topic: Estimate-revision momentum: how upward EPS/revenue revision breadth leads price via the post-forecast-revision drift, and why breadth + price-confirmation beats a lone divergence
recent.summary: Analyst estimate revisions are a genuine, well-documented fundamental predictor: prices underreact to revisions and DRIFT in their direction for roughly six months (the post-forecast-revision drift, PFRD). Old evidence (Givoly/Lakonishok-era) put the up-minus-down revision portfolio spread near ~3% annually, and later work finds aggregated revisions can predict post-earnings-announcement returns as well as or better than the earnings surprise itself. The mechanism is the reason it persists and is the key to trading it: the DIRECTION of revisions is far more persistent than the direction of returns because analysts themselves underreact — anchoring-and-adjustment and herding make them revise incrementally and insufficiently, so a first up-revision statistically predicts more up-revisions (Chen et al. 2020, JBFA). Signal quality is not uniform. A single revision is mostly noise, and noise/bias in analyst forecasts rises with the forecast horizon (Noise in Expectations, RFS 2024), so BREADTH — how many analysts are raising vs cutting over ~100 days — and NEAR-TERM (next-quarter/next-FY) revisions carry the real signal, not one far-out number. Consistency matters more than magnitude: high-innovation revisions that are CONSISTENT with the prior trend and with price action drive more drift than larger 'reversal' revisions that fight the tape (Chen 2025), and revisions that merely drift toward existing consensus ('low-innovation') carry little information. recent.how_to_apply: Treat fundamental_screen.top_upward_revisions and revision_direction=up / positive eps_growth_next_yr_pct as a real candidate lane, not background noise — this is the direct fix for repeatedly defaulting MU-type names to the watchlist and eating +15% regret_misses. When underwriting one, weight BREADTH of near-term (30-day EPS / next-Q) revisions over any single number, and require the revision trend to be consistent (up-revisions following up-revisions), because that persistence is where the edge lives. For the fat pitch, demand price CONFIRMATION of the fundamentals — positive rel_strength_1m/3m, no_supply_pullback or a reclaim — which is precisely the post_earnings_drift_candidate gap_held_revisions_up read; that revisions-and-price-AGREE case gets full weight and can clear the bar now. recent.topic: Exit on pre-committed invalidators, not real-time conviction: the disposition effect, 'resulting', and why the written plan (not the mood) must license every early exit
recent.summary: My single binding process_fail is HPE: I closed a LOSING position ahead of its stop on a 'conviction crack,' graded process_fail with tag missing_invalidators_on_plan. The behavioral literature explains why that class of decision loses systematically. Odean's canonical study of 10,000 brokerage accounts (Journal of Finance 53:1775-1798, 1998) documents the disposition effect: investors are 1.5-2x more likely to sell a winner than a loser, and crucially this is NOT justified by subsequent returns - the losers they clung to did not go on to outperform, so the discretionary exit judgment was simply wrong on average. The practitioner consensus fix is pre-commitment: a 1991 study found the disposition effect weakens sharply when people sell at predetermined rules/intervals instead of discretionarily, and the reliable antidotes are predefined exit rules set BEFORE entry, mechanical stop/target execution, and documenting the rationale so the exit is a rule-check rather than a fresh emotional decision. Annie Duke's 'resulting' sharpens this: judging a decision by its outcome corrupts learning, so you must write the reasoning and the expected outcome distribution up front and grade the exit against THAT, not against the P&L - which is exactly why DELL (stop fired as planned, still a loss) is a process_win while HPE (discretionary, happened to save a few dollars) is a process_fail. recent.how_to_apply: Treat the validator-enforced thesis_invalidators (invalidating_print, invalidating_structure, time_box) as the ONLY licensed early-exit reasons: before closing any holding ahead of its stop, name which specific invalidator fired and cite the observable print or structure - if none did and it is only conviction wobble, HOLD and let the stop/chandelier trail do its job, because that is the exact HPE process_fail I must not repeat. Grade every exit against the entry plan, not the P&L (Duke's resulting): a stop firing as written is a process_win even at a loss, a discretionary save is a process_fail. For winners, beat the cut-them-early disposition reflex mechanically - bank with sell_fraction (~0.4-0.6) at >=2R and trail the rest under structure while invalidators stay clear, per KB-2388376284's chandelier point and the runner playbook. Q1 fundamentals (revenue $23.4B, net income $965M) confirm profitable scale, and the current tape ('Dell Stock Nears Buy Point') shows institutional demand building. With no earnings until 9/3, a 45-day swing captures the momentum leg without event risk.

HPE is the most valuation-protected way to own the AI-server/networking buildout in a tape where reaccelerating inflation (CPI 4.27%) and a rising 10-year (4.56%) are punishing rich multiples. It trades at just ~12.2x forward earnings and 1.67x sales - the cheapest in the server group - after a record fiscal Q2 and the completed Juniper acquisition, which adds a scaled networking franchise. recent.note: Weekly self-review: Last Friday's stated change was to name the specific thesis_invalidator that fired before any discretionary SELL_TO_CLOSE, instead of a full close on cracked conviction -- I cannot grade whether it worked, because the book stayed 100% flat all week (zero opens, zero closes) and never produced a discretionary exit to test it against; the honest read is 'not exercised,' not 'followed.' The track record is unchanged from last week: still just 2 closed trades (DELL -$13.52, HPE -$4.53, total -$18.05), still anecdote-phase calibration, so no new hard rules to draw. What went right: the book avoided forcing a mediocre trade for a seventh straight day, and this afternoon's risk desk correctly vetoed a UNP BUY that looked clean on the surface -- a real Q2 beat plus a real same-day Canadian National rail-access agreement supporting the pending Norfolk Southern deal. What went wrong was reasoning, not data: the vetoed proposal's own thesis stated the CN agreement was 'signed one day earlier' when every dated headline in the bundle for that story was same-session (age_days 0.2-0.6, all 2026-07-24), and it cited a favorable RBC note from the same news pull while omitting a same-pull BNSF headline publicly attacking the exact merger-approval mechanism the trade was built on -- an unforced, checkable error that the risk desk had to catch instead of the reasoning process catching it first. The one change for next week: before finalizing any BUY thesis, I will explicitly cross-check every dated or sequenced claim in the catalysts and thesis fields against the actual age_days/published timestamps of the supporting headlines in the bundle, and label the timing as unverified rather than asserting a sequence the data doesn't support -- next Friday's review grades whether that habit actually prevented a repeat of this exact failure mode.

Weekly self-review: Last Friday's stated change was to get the insider Form-4 feed pre-classified into sponsor/10b5-1 vs. discretionary officer transactions instead of handing me hundreds of noisy rows -- that fix landed and it worked: tonight's insider_activity block gave clean, directly actionable signals (BSX bullish_cluster_buying, 3 officers buying $554K with zero sells; ZS notable_discretionary_selling), a real improvement over last week's noise. The trading result this week was rougher: my only two closed trades, DELL and HPE, both lost (-$135 and -$45, 0% win rate, avg R -0.98), and with only 2 closed trades this is anecdote-level evidence per my own sample-size rules -- I am not inventing hard rules from it, but the pattern is worth naming honestly. Both losses shared the same demand_driver (hyperscaler_server_capex/servers_hardware) dressed up as two separate theses when the actual catalyst language ('SMCI collapse consolidates AI-server share') was nearly identical -- bad reasoning (thin diversification), not bad data, and it is exactly the clustering the system's theme-risk cap now exists to prevent. HPE's exit was graded process_fail: I closed it at $46.08 without its $43.75 stop being hit and without a clearly named invalidator firing -- conviction cracked, not thesis broken, which is the discretionary-exit mistake I need to stop making. What I got right: after those two losses on 7/15, the book stayed disciplined and all-cash through the rest of the week, including declining a real-looking AMD dip-buy today because my own stated trigger condition (post-event confirmation) was not actually met. A new engineering issue surfaced tonight -- a validator-clean UNH proposal was rejected at execution with 'insufficient cash' on a 100%-cash account, which needs an engineering look, not a reasoning fix. The one change for next week: before any discretionary SELL_TO_CLOSE that isn't a stop or horizon exit, I will name the specific thesis_invalidator that actually fired in the sell thesis itself -- if none of the three stated invalidators fired, the move is to hold or trim with sell_fraction, not a full discretionary close.

universe_scan.note: light run - no universe scan this cycle

filing_texts_note: Real MD&A and press-release prose per focus ticker. When earnings_release.contains_guidance_language is true, QUOTE the specific guidance sentence (numbers and fiscal period) instead of paraphrasing. mdna.section == 'document_start' means general filing text, not MD&A.

fundamental_screen.note: Full-universe estimate screen, refreshed pre-market (6am/9am ET, gated on true America/New_York time). top_upward_revisions = fundamental inflections regardless of price - candidates the momentum funnel may not surface. estimate_changes_since_previous = what moved THIS MORNING (earnings/guidance). Each row may carry revision_direction (up/down/flat), eps_growth_next_yr_pct (forward EPS growth), and eps_estimate_current_yr / eps_estimate_next_yr (current/next fiscal-year EPS estimates - the scanner's fwd_pe_est divides last close by the current-year figure) - judge a multiple against growth, not news tone.

todays_8ks.note: 8-K filings TODAY across the ENTIRE universe (one EDGAR index sweep). An 8-K on a non-focus name may be the day's real opportunity - pull the filing with WebFetch if the form looks material before dismissing it.

stack_cards.note: Supply-chain differential cards for THIS run's focus set. Answer differential_question in thesis when proposing a BUY.

financial_checklists.note: Per-focus-name financial-line checklists by business model. Use the weight line: different models, different scoreboards.

concept_memory.note: Durable concept memory for focus names — what they do, how to score them, and lessons appended from research/exits/shadows. Prefer this over reinventing the business each run; update via new lessons only.
